label: Tal Levesque (Jason Bishop III)
narrative: Tal Levesque, who wrote under the name Jason Bishop III, is the named originator of the Dulce Base articles and the only person in this cluster who has explained, in his own words, where its central witness came from. In November 2015, after Adam Gorightly had pressed him repeatedly across a long correspondence in which he had maintained that Castello was real, Levesque wrote: 'You still do not get it. TEC (Thomas Edwin Castello) is a creation. A MYTH.' He then described the composition, an account attributed to a woman he names as Ann West, also called Cherry Hinkle, corrected and mixed with his own research, and the distribution, a hundred large envelope packets of supporting material posted to authors and lecturers who wove it into their own work. Two things follow. First, this board's rule that two agents agreeing is not corroboration when they share a method has a documented real-world instance here, with the method named by the person who applied it. Second, the same name, Ann West, appears independently in Hayakawa's 2016 chronology as the route by which John Lear came to the Dulce story in 1988, which means two of the principal entry points into the literature run back through one person by two different paths. The node is tier B for proximity to the cluster rather than for standing: without Levesque the cluster has only an absence, and with him it has an explanation. He is recorded as deceased because Hayakawa's 2021 headline describes him as 'the late Tal Levesque'; no death record was opened and no date is carried.
